why: `eval` runs its code where it is, in the workspace around it, once its argument is evaluated: after the code before it and before the code after it (MATLAB doc 'eval'), and a script runs in its caller's workspace, so what it assigns is a variable there once it has run (MATLAB doc 'Scripts vs. Functions'; the project's script-workspace rule, src/resolution/matlab-script-workspace.ts: a bare name's failed call that a script run strictly before it makes is kept dormant). So in `runner.m` and `runner2.m` the script `mkvars` the text runs makes `XV` before `XV(2)` reads it: dormant; in `runner3.m` the text reads `XV(2)` before the statement runs the script: a call of nothing, failed. Code given in literal pieces is read where each piece writes it, as one literal is (found by the step 14 second review, which saw the concatenation answer the other way round from a literal).
